content: Immunoglobulin-binding protein 1 (IGBP1) is a protein encoded by the IGBP1 gene in humans. The proliferation and differentiation of B cells rely on the activity of the B-cell antigen receptor (BCR) complex. When antigens bind to specific B-cell receptors, this interaction triggers a tyrosine phosphorylation reaction mediated through the BCR complex. This phosphorylation event subsequently activates multiple intracellular signal transduction pathways. IGBP1 has been demonstrated to interact with several phosphatases, including PPP4C (protein phosphatase 4 catalytic subunit), PPP6C (protein phosphatase 6 catalytic subunit), and PPP2CA (protein phosphatase 2 catalytic subunit alpha isoform).
